title: Liquid AI Pricing: Models and API Costs (2026 Guide)
summary: Liquid AI pricing in 2026 varies by plan. Understand the costs for each tier so you can select the option that fits your budget.
body_markdown:
## Connecting the Liquid API to workflows with Activepieces


Out of Activepieces' 747 integrations, none needs to be Liquid-specific, because[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) can call Liquid AI's hosted API through its generic HTTP request step.


Its credit allowance caps how many automated calls you can pay for in a month. That ceiling matters less than the approval step in front of any call that sends text to a customer.


Below is a two-step example workflow: a trigger flows into a single HTTP request that sends a POST with an Authorization header and a body. A Liquid call would be built the same way.


On the left-hand side, the run details show each step's input and output. When a call returns something odd, you can see exactly what was sent and what came back before anyone blames the model.


*(screenshot sits here)*


### What the plan costs


Pick a plan and you've set the monthly ceiling on this automation. According to[Activepieces' own pricing guide](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/activepieces-cloud-pricing-plans-2026-price-guide) , Cloud costs $0 a month on Free with 1,000 credits, $20 on Plus with 10,000 credits, and $200 on Team with 50,000 credits.


Anyone needing more than 1,000 monthly credits must therefore pay at least $20. Free's enough to test one workflow against real tickets, but a busy inbox will exhaust it.


Plus works out to $0.002 per credit. Team works out to $0.004, so moving up buys more volume at **double the per-credit rate, not a discount** . Those totals are Activepieces' fee only, and Liquid's usage charges come on top.


A wrongly worded refund promise sent to an angry customer costs far more than the minutes a reviewer spends checking a draft, so put a human approval step before any action that can't be undone.


Cap the number of runs as well, so a loop or a flood of retries can't drain credits unnoticed overnight.


Figures were read from Activepieces' pages on 2026-11-09.
